findings: CLI main -p./-i. branches reject any value starting with minus before setValue. This narrows prior negative-input concerns: these CLI branches do not pass ordinary negative values. Positive out-of-range values reach the unvalidated integer setter; no native executable was run.

SearchParams binds dht range0..65, vradix1..24 and mm1..INT_MAX to SET_INT. The CLI branch has no numeric range check, so e.g. mm=0 and dht=66 are not rejected by this traced assignment path. Algorithm behavior on those values remains a separate obligation.

Scanner tests depend on external TEST_DATA_DIR. They assert unique emitted path counts:200,190 after ten skipped paths, one image/video, and one allowed truncated JPEG. QSet collection does not prove exactly one signal per file or descriptor correctness.

Scanner destructor test intentionally starts no event loop and expects zero emitted items. It proves neither completion nor preservation of active processed-but-uncommitted work. No unreadable-subtree/reconciliation error gate is asserted in this file.
Skip-list tests expect nonexistent paths to remain in skip. This supports skip-set semantics but does not establish that Engine may safely remove remaining index records after incomplete traversal.

TestBase reads full CSV into memory and splits commas, with , substitution; no general quoted CSV parser. Numeric test fields convert without success flags. Data-row positive count required; dataset source existence and actual values remain unverified.
